To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the integration of metabolic and regulatory networks is a challenging task but that it is possible to achieve this integration by using a variety of approaches.

(1) the integration of genome-scale models of metabolism and gene regulation is a promising approach for understanding microbial systems; (2) the development of such integrated models requires the integration of data and models at different scales, and the use of appropriate algorithms to achieve this; and (3) the use of integrated models will be critical for understanding the complex regulatory-metabolic systems that govern microbial physiology.

(i) we have integrated regulatory and metabolic models to predict the behavior of microbial systems; (ii) we have used these integrated models to predict the effect of genetic and environmental perturbations on cellular behavior; (iii) we have used the integrated models to predict gene essentiality; (iv) we have used integrated models to predict growth phenotypes; and (v) we have developed a new approach for integrating regulatory and metabolic networks that is applicable to all microbes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction and application of integrated regulatory-metabolite models for the study of microbial systems.
the development of new computational methods for the integration of large-scale data sets into predictive and mechanistic models of biological systems.
the construction, analysis and simulation of large-scale integrated metabolic and regulatory networks.

the time has come for the construction of integrated regulatory-metaboloic models of microbes.
the time has arrived for the construction of genome-scale integrated regulatory and metabolic networks.
